---
title: "Readings — Anatomy of a library molecule"
---

The papers here are about the parts of the molecule and about what each part was invented to
solve. Read them with the construct from the deck beside you, and label every sequence they
print.

## The molecule and its parts

**Meyer M, Kircher M (2010).** *Illumina sequencing library preparation for highly
multiplexed target capture and sequencing.* Cold Spring Harbor Protocols 2010:pdb.prot5448.
[doi:10.1101/pdb.prot5448](https://doi.org/10.1101/pdb.prot5448) — **start here**

> A bench protocol that spells out every part of the library: adapters, index PCR primers,
> what each oligo is for. Find P5, P7, the primer sites and the index in the oligo table and
> draw the product.

**Kircher M, Sawyer S, Meyer M (2012).** *Double indexing overcomes inaccuracies in
multiplex sequencing on the Illumina platform.* Nucleic Acids Research 40:e3.
[doi:10.1093/nar/gkr771](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkr771) — **start here**

> Why a single index is not enough, shown with data. Look for how two indexes catch
> misassigned reads, and for what the index reads cost in cycles.

**Costello M, et al. (2018).** *Characterization and remediation of sample index swaps by
non-redundant dual indexing on massively parallel sequencing platforms.* BMC Genomics
19:332. [doi:10.1186/s12864-018-4703-0](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12864-018-4703-0)

> Index swapping measured, and where it comes from: free adapter or primer in the pool.
> Connects the architecture of the molecule to the clean-up steps that protect it.

## Transposase-based libraries

**Adey A, et al. (2010).** *Rapid, low-input, low-bias construction of shotgun fragment
libraries by high-density in vitro transposition.* Genome Biology 11:R119.
[doi:10.1186/gb-2010-11-12-r119](https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2010-11-12-r119)

> The paper behind Nextera. Note how the transposon end becomes part of the Read 1 and Read 2
> sites, and what the gap-filling and PCR have to do afterwards.

**Picelli S, et al. (2014).** *Tn5 transposase and tagmentation procedures for massively
scaled sequencing projects.* Genome Research 24:2033–2040.
[doi:10.1101/gr.177881.114](https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.177881.114)

> The do-it-yourself version: loading Tn5 with two different adapters, and the consequences
> for the fraction of usable fragments.

## Information in the reads

**Zheng GXY, et al. (2017).** *Massively parallel digital transcriptional profiling of
single cells.* Nature Communications 8:14049.
[doi:10.1038/ncomms14049](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms14049)

> The 10x 3′ construct: find the barcode, the UMI, the poly(dT) and the read structure.

**Kivioja T, et al. (2012).** *Counting absolute numbers of molecules using unique molecular
identifiers.* Nature Methods 9:72–74.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.1778](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.1778)

> What a UMI does and where it has to sit. Short.

**Parkhomchuk D, et al. (2009).** *Transcriptome analysis by strand-specific sequencing of
complementary DNA.* Nucleic Acids Research 37:e123.
[doi:10.1093/nar/gkp596](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkp596)

> dUTP marking of the second strand: how strand information survives in a library.
